pages.text: Laundry day made a mountain of quilts. Kota tried to lift the biggest one alone. It toppled right over them.
Only two legs waved in the air. "Where's Kota?" Dad lifted the quilt. Kota popped out, breathing hard.
"I wanted to carry it all by myself." Kota glared at the bundle. It would not move.
A bull passing by grinned. Dad handed Kota one end. "Let's play Heave Together. Together, it's light!"
They held an end each and lifted. "It went up! It's only half as heavy!" Kota's eyes shone.
At the clothesline, the bull took another end. All three lifted together. The quilt felt light as a feather.
The quilts flapped on the line in the wind. Every one was hanging up! Kota's tail rose proudly.
The bull lifted Kota onto his shoulders. "Well done, little helper!" Higher than the clothesline, Kota laughed.
"One, ask for help! Two, hold it together! Three, heave!" The heavy load felt only a quarter as heavy now.
Dad touched his forehead to Kota's and hugged them. Even Kota's heart felt lighter. Dangling from Dad's arms, Kota called, "Together, it's light!"
